deities: Goddess Baglamukhi (Pitambara Devi - one of the ten Mahavidyas, main deity)

history.dynasty: Modern - founded by Shree Swami Ji Maharaj (unknown origins; a Dandi sannyasi)
history.period: Founded 1929 (main Baglamukhi deity installed 1935); early 20th century
history.summary: Shri Pitambara Peeth is a major Shakti pilgrimage center at Datia dedicated to Goddess Baglamukhi, one of the ten Mahavidyas; 'Pitambara' means 'the one adorned in yellow'. The shrine's story began in 1929 when a young sannyasi called Swami Ji stopped in Datia for one night, was impressed by its Sanskrit scholars, stayed for five years of tapasya, and then established the ashram; the main Baglamukhi deity was installed in 1935 and he remained until his samadhi in June 1979 (founding-date reports vary between 1929 and the 1920s). The complex also houses a rare temple to Goddess Dhumavati (another Mahavidya), plus shrines to Parshuram, Hanuman and Kal Bhairav, a Haridra Sarovar, and a Sanskrit library; it is maintained by a trust and known for Sanskrit education work. CSV state-column error: the source CSV lists the town in the 'state' column - the site is in Madhya Pradesh, not a town called 'Madhya Pradesh'. (verify) Exact darshan hours vary across sources; the gokshetra darshan guide notes the temple's own website warns about copycat websites.

name: Pitambara Peeth
town_description: Datia is a historic town in northern Madhya Pradesh, about 25 km from Jhansi, known for the 17th-century Datia Palace (Bir Singh Palace) and as a Shakti-pilgrimage hub with the Pitambara Peeth and the Jain hill complex of Sonagiri nearby.

travel.airport: Gwalior Airport is the nearest major airport (~70-75 km - verify); Jhansi is the common rail/road gateway.
travel.railway: Datia Railway Station is very close to the Peeth; Virangna Lakshmibai (Jhansi) Junction is ~45 minutes away with broad connectivity.
travel.road: On the Gwalior-Jhansi corridor (NH 44/AH43 area); local buses run from Jhansi (~50-80 Rs per person per reviews) or hire a taxi (~1500 Rs return, per traveler reviews - verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for comfortable weather; Navratri and Saturdays draw the largest crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reviews report darshan from about 5:00 AM to about 9:00 PM (verify - hours conflict across sources); weekday darshan 15-30 minutes, longer queues on Saturdays and festival days.
